overview.description: Card Bingo is a lottery-style card game where players try to match called cards to their hand. A caller draws cards and announces them; players turn down matching cards in their hand. First player to turn down all cards wins. Similar to traditional number Bingo but using playing cards.

history.origins: Card Bingo adapts the traditional number-based Bingo lottery game to use standard playing cards. The basic concept of matching called items to a card grid translates naturally to matching called cards to a hand. Various versions have evolved with different dealing patterns, betting structures, and win conditions.
timeline: Traditional Bingo: Lottery game with numbered balls/grid cards
Card adaptation: Playing cards used instead of numbers
Evolution: Multiple variants developed with betting, jackpots, high-low scoring
Current: Played socially and in clubs (e.g., Doncaster Whist Club version with 60 players)
history.evolution: Started as simple matching game. Variants added: 13-card version for larger groups, suit-ignored version (call rank only), betting rounds, jackpot accumulation, high-low split pots, and Canadian variant with payment for uncalled cards.
history.cultural: Played in social clubs and homes. The Doncaster Whist Club version with 60 players uses multiple tables. Also known as Bango! or Hoy! in some regions (based on the win call).

setup.players: Basic game: up to 10 players plus caller. Large groups: 60+ players possible with multiple decks and tables. Caller can be a player or dedicated.
setup.deck: Basic: Two standard 52-card packs without jokers (one for dealing, one for calling). Large groups: Multiple packs as needed. Some variants use one deck with suits ignored.
setup.equipment: 2+ decks of cards, chips/money for betting variants
setup.dealing: Basic: 5 cards face up to each player (6 cards if 8 or fewer players). One pack used for dealing. Second pack used by caller. Thirteen-card version: 13 cards each for larger games.

rules.objective: Be the first player to have all your cards called/turned face down.
rules.gameplay: Caller draws cards one at a time from the calling pack and announces rank and suit (e.g., 'five of diamonds'). Players who hold the called card turn it face down. First player to turn all cards face down calls 'Bingo!' (or 'Bango!'/'Hoy!') and wins. If playing for money, winner's hand is checked against the calling pack to verify all cards were called.
keyRules: Two packs: one for dealing, one for calling
Cards dealt face up (basic) or face down (some variants)
Caller announces rank and suit (or just rank in suit-ignored variants)
First to turn all cards down wins
Winner's hand verified against calling pack in gambling games

strategy.basic: Pure luck game - no decisions to make. Hope your cards are called early.
strategy.intermediate: In betting variants, assess pot odds. In high-low variants, understand which cards help for high vs low.
strategy.advanced: Card counting in multi-deck games to estimate probability of your remaining cards being called. In betting round variants, read opponent patterns.
tips: Basic game is pure chance - enjoy the social aspect
In jackpot variants, consider pot size vs probability
High-low variants: picture cards good for high, aces flexible
With multiple decks, duplicate cards in hand are possible

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck comprising four suits: Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, and Spades. Each suit contains thirteen ranks: Ace, 2 through 10, Jack, Queen, and King, providing versatile options for various card games.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card iconography and distinct color coding for easy identification.
engine.rankDescription: Standard thirteen ranks per suit: Ace, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack, Queen, and King, where each rank has distinct value and meaning depending on the specific game rules and player strategies.
